phase1_business.problem: A card issuer runs one undifferentiated marketing programme across its entire active book. Campaign response is measured in aggregate, so spend is allocated uniformly to ~9k cardholders whose behaviour is anything but uniform.
phase1_business.business_objective: Discover a small, stable set of behavioural segments in six months of card activity, so credit-line, retention and cross-sell offers can be targeted per segment rather than broadcast.
phase1_business.data_mining_goal: Unsupervised partitioning of cardholders into k segments (2 <= k <= 12) that are internally compact, well separated, reproducible under resampling, and describable in plain language to a marketing stakeholder.
phase1_business.why_unsupervised: No labelled 'segment' target exists and none can be manufactured without begging the question. Success is therefore judged by internal validity, replication stability and business interpretability - never by accuracy.

success_criteria.rationale: Above the 0.25 'weak but real structure' band; behavioural data rarely exceeds 0.5.

success_criteria.criterion: Bootstrap cluster-wise Jaccard >= 0.60 for every retained segment
success_criteria.rationale: Hennig (2007) calls <0.60 'dissolved'; a segment we cannot reproduce cannot be budgeted against.

success_criteria.criterion: Mean bootstrap ARI (Hubert & Arabie 1985) >= 0.60 for the partition
success_criteria.rationale: Partition-level replication; guards against a lucky seed.

success_criteria.criterion: No segment below 3% of the book
success_criteria.rationale: A segment too small to staff a campaign for is an outlier bucket, not a market.

success_criteria.criterion: Surrogate decision tree (depth<=4) reproduces >= 85% of assignments
success_criteria.rationale: If a 4-rule tree can restate the model, marketing can act on it without the model.

success_criteria.criterion: Inductive scoring path < 5 ms/record at p95
success_criteria.rationale: Segment must be assignable in the offer-decisioning service, not just in a notebook.

stakeholders.needs: Named, sized, actionable segments and an offer per segment.
Assurance that segments are not a proxy for a protected attribute.
A deterministic, versioned, monitorable scoring artifact.

constraints_and_risks: Six months of behaviour only - no seasonality can be modelled, and TENURE is near-constant (87% at 12).
The file carries no demographics; segments are behavioural, and must not be presented as customer identity.

Internal validity indices are biased toward small k (Milligan & Cooper 1985), so the search objective is explicitly regularised for balance and minimum segment size rather than left to maximise silhouette alone.
Monetary features are heavy-tailed and unbounded; without a variance-stabilising transform the solution collapses to 'one whale cluster plus everyone else'.

charter_revision.argument: No pipeline in the shortlist satisfies SC-1 and SC-2 together, and the reason is structural rather than incidental. Every candidate that clears the silhouette bar does so by abstaining on roughly a fifth of the book and carving out a tight core, which leaves a small segment that does not survive resampling. Every candidate whose segments all reproduce lands just under the bar. The 0.25 threshold was set before the data was opened, from a general rule of thumb about weak structure; the evidence now says the achievable ceiling for a fully reproducible partition on this book is the value above. Revising SC-1 to that ceiling is a change of expectation supported by measurement. Relaxing SC-2 instead would mean campaigning against a segment that a different sample of the same customers would not produce.
charter_revision.recommendation: Deploy the most stable high-objective pipeline, record SC-1 as failed against the original bar, and take the revised threshold back to the business owner as a Phase-1 amendment rather than presenting it as a pass.

charter_compliance.verdict: No candidate satisfies every criterion. The separation and stability criteria are in direct tension on this data, and the charter needs an amendment.

profiles.thesis: Heavy purchase volume settled in full - interchange-rich, interest-poor. The most valuable and the most poachable segment on the book.
profiles.action: Protect with rewards and a proactive limit increase. Never target with balance-transfer offers; it reads as a downgrade.

profiles.thesis: Carries a persistent balance against a meaningful limit and rarely settles in full. The core net-interest-margin segment.
profiles.action: Retention pricing and a fixed-instalment conversion offer. Monitor utilisation drift as an early-warning signal.

profiles.thesis: Uses the card as a liquidity line rather than a payment instrument. The highest credit risk and the highest fee income per account on the book.
profiles.action: Do not upsell spend. Offer a structured personal loan at a lower APR to refinance the balance, and set a cash-advance velocity alert.

profiles.thesis: Minimal spend, minimal balance, card effectively idle. Costs more to service than it earns.
profiles.action: Low-cost reactivation only - a single targeted first-purchase incentive, then let attrition run rather than spending against it.

profiles.thesis: Large granted line, comfortable balance, spend well below what the limit implies. Wallet share is going somewhere else.
profiles.action: Category-specific accelerators to win back share of wallet; premium product migration.

model_details.name: Credit-card behavioural segmentation
model_details.type: Unsupervised clustering pipeline (preprocessing + clusterer + induced nearest-centroid assigner)
model_details.pipeline: raw17 | knn5 | wins=0.995 | yeojohnson | minmax | pca_var80  ->  minibatch_kmeans k=5 n_init=20
model_details.selected_by: Hill-climbing CASH search over a 3,435,696-configuration space, 120 evaluations

intended_use.primary: Allocating marketing, retention and credit-line treatments across an existing active credit-card book.
intended_use.users: Portfolio marketing analysts and the campaign decisioning service.
out_of_scope: Credit decisioning, pricing, or any adverse action. The segments are descriptive of behaviour and were never validated against repayment outcomes.
Individual-level inference about a customer's circumstances. A segment is a statistical neighbourhood, not a fact about a person.
Any use on a population other than active cardholders with >= 6 months tenure.

factors.relevant: Behavioural only: spend, balance, cash advance, repayment, product mix.
factors.not_present: The source file carries no demographic, geographic or protected attributes, so the model cannot condition on them directly.
factors.proxy_risk: Absence of protected attributes is not evidence of absence of disparate impact - credit limit and cash-advance reliance are both plausible proxies for income and, through it, for protected classes. A disparate-impact review against the issuer's own demographic data is a precondition of production use, and cannot be done from this file.

model_card.evaluation_data: Same book. There is no held-out period; the source file is a single six-month snapshot with no time index, which is a real limitation.
ethical_considerations: Segment names are operational shorthand. 'Cash-Advance Reliant' describes an observed behaviour, not a judgement about the customer, and must not surface in any customer-facing message.

The 'Dormant / Low-Engagement' action explicitly recommends limiting spend on reactivation. Applied without care this becomes systematic under-service of a group that may correlate with income - it needs a human sign-off, not an automated rule.
Assignments near a segment boundary flip between refreshes; the artifact exposes an explicit confidence flag so those accounts can be excluded from treatment.
caveats_and_recommendations: Six months of behaviour, no seasonality. A book scored in a promotional quarter will drift; the monitor is the mitigation, not the fix.
Silhouette in the reduced modelling space overstates separation relative to the reference space; both numbers are reported and the reference-space value is the one to quote externally.

Re-fit cadence: quarterly, or immediately on a drift alert. Segment identifiers are not stable across refits - map new segments to old by centroid nearest-match and publish the mapping, or campaign histories become uninterpretable.

success_criteria_results.rationale: Above the 0.25 'weak but real structure' band; behavioural data rarely exceeds 0.5.
success_criteria_results.evidence: silhouette = 0.239 in the reference space (0.240 in the modelling space)

success_criteria_results.criterion: Bootstrap cluster-wise Jaccard >= 0.60 for every retained segment
success_criteria_results.rationale: Hennig (2007) calls <0.60 'dissolved'; a segment we cannot reproduce cannot be budgeted against.

success_criteria_results.criterion: Mean bootstrap ARI (Hubert & Arabie 1985) >= 0.60 for the partition
success_criteria_results.rationale: Partition-level replication; guards against a lucky seed.

success_criteria_results.criterion: No segment below 3% of the book
success_criteria_results.rationale: A segment too small to staff a campaign for is an outlier bucket, not a market.
success_criteria_results.evidence: smallest segment holds 15.3% of the book

success_criteria_results.criterion: Surrogate decision tree (depth<=4) reproduces >= 85% of assignments
success_criteria_results.rationale: If a 4-rule tree can restate the model, marketing can act on it without the model.

success_criteria_results.criterion: Inductive scoring path < 5 ms/record at p95
success_criteria_results.rationale: Segment must be assignable in the offer-decisioning service, not just in a notebook.
success_criteria_results.evidence: p95 scoring latency = 0.012 ms/record at batch 1000

personas.action: Protect with rewards and a proactive limit increase. Never target with balance-transfer offers; it reads as a downgrade.
Retention pricing and a fixed-instalment conversion offer. Monitor utilisation drift as an early-warning signal.
Do not upsell spend. Offer a structured personal loan at a lower APR to refinance the balance, and set a cash-advance velocity alert.
Low-cost reactivation only - a single targeted first-purchase incentive, then let attrition run rather than spending against it.
Category-specific accelerators to win back share of wallet; premium product migration.

latency.note: Single-process, cold cache excluded, no network or feature-store hop.

citations.authors: Wirth, R. & Hipp, J.
citations.title: CRISP-DM: Towards a Standard Process Model for Data Mining
citations.venue: Proc. 4th Int. Conf. Practical Applications of Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
citations.used_for: The six-phase structure of the whole project and of the dashboard.
citations.implemented_in: package layout; config.BUSINESS_CHARTER, data.py, prepare.py, autoresearch.py, evaluate.py, deploy.py
citations.deviation: The phase loop is executed once end-to-end and logged, rather than iterated informally. Every backward arrow that would normally be tacit (a data-quality finding changing the preparation step) is recorded as an explicit resolution in the audit ledger.

citations.authors: Thornton, C., Hutter, F., Hoos, H. H. & Leyton-Brown, K.
citations.title: Auto-WEKA: Combined Selection and Hyperparameter Optimization of Classification Algorithms
citations.used_for: The CASH formulation - treating algorithm choice as one more dimension of the hyperparameter space rather than an outer loop.
citations.implemented_in: search_space.SPACE (algorithm is a searched dimension); search_space.CONDITIONS encodes the conditional structure
citations.deviation: Supervised CASH has a loss with an unbiased held-out estimate. Clustering has neither, so the objective is an internal index and the whole result rests on the index being a reasonable proxy - a substantially weaker guarantee, and the reason the evaluation phase leans on stability instead.

citations.authors: Tschechlov, D., Fritz, M. & Schwarz, H.
citations.title: AutoML4Clust: Efficient AutoML for Clustering Analyses
citations.used_for: Carrying CASH to unsupervised learning; optimising CVIs (SIL, CH, DB) as the objective; and the subsample-then-refit cost control.
citations.implemented_in: autoresearch.Evaluator (search runs on SearchConfig.search_subsample, champion refit on the full book); metrics.score_partition
citations.deviation: The paper compares random search, Bayesian optimisation, Hyperband and BOHB, and searches algorithm + k. This project searches the preprocessing chain as well - on heavy-tailed financial data the transform choice moves the objective more than the algorithm does - and uses hill climbing with random search as the control arm.

citations.authors: Treder-Tschechlov, D., Fritz, M., Schwarz, H. & Mitschang, B.
citations.title: ML2DAC: Meta-Learning to Democratize AutoML for Clustering Analysis
citations.used_for: The argument that CVI *selection* is itself a decision that biases the result, which motivates the calibrated composite over a single index.
citations.deviation: ML2DAC learns which CVI to use from a meta-knowledge base of prior datasets. No such base exists here, so the three indices are combined with fixed, stated weights instead of selected - simpler, and honest about the fact that the weighting is a judgement.

citations.authors: Hutter, F., Hoos, H. & Leyton-Brown, K.
citations.title: An Efficient Approach for Assessing Hyperparameter Importance
citations.used_for: Attributing objective variance to individual search dimensions - which decisions in the pipeline actually mattered.
citations.deviation: fANOVA fits a random forest over the space and marginalises properly. This is a one-way eta-squared over observed trials, which is cheaper and biased by the optimiser's own sampling. The random-search arm is pooled in to dilute that bias, and the panel states the caveat rather than hiding it.

citations.authors: Glover, F.
citations.title: Future Paths for Integer Programming and Links to Artificial Intelligence
citations.used_for: Short-term memory preventing the climber from cycling on a plateau.
citations.deviation: Attribute-level tabu tenure is replaced by whole-configuration hashing, which is coarser but exact for a conditional space where 'the same attribute' is not always well defined.

citations.authors: Selman, B., Levesque, H. & Mitchell, D.
citations.title: A New Method for Solving Hard Satisfiability Problems
citations.used_for: Sideways (non-worsening) moves as the mechanism for crossing plateaus, and random restarts as the mechanism for escaping local optima.
citations.deviation: Plateaus here come from categorical dimensions with no effect on the current pipeline (e.g. changing `init` under a non-KMeans algorithm), so the sideways budget is small and per-restart.

citations.authors: Mladenovic, N. & Hansen, P.
citations.title: Variable Neighborhood Search
citations.used_for: Biasing neighbourhood sampling toward dimensions that have historically produced improvements.
citations.deviation: Formal VNS systematically enlarges the neighbourhood radius; here the radius stays at one dimension and only the sampling distribution adapts.

citations.authors: Coello Coello, C. A.
citations.title: Theoretical and Numerical Constraint-Handling Techniques used with Evolutionary Algorithms
citations.venue: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 191(11-12)
citations.used_for: Static-penalty constraint handling, so that any feasible solution strictly dominates any infeasible one while infeasible ones keep a gradient.
citations.deviation: None material. The shift is set to the maximum attainable raw objective (1.0), which makes the ordering exactly lexicographic.

citations.authors: Rousseeuw, P. J.
citations.title: Silhouettes: A Graphical Aid to the Interpretation and Validation of Cluster Analysis
citations.venue: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics 20
citations.used_for: Primary internal index and the per-sample silhouette diagnostic.
citations.deviation: Computed on a seeded subsample above 2,500 points (the index is O(n^2)). The dashboard shows the per-cluster distribution, not only the mean, because that is what Rousseeuw's original diagnostic is for.

citations.authors: Calinski, T. & Harabasz, J.
citations.title: A Dendrite Method for Cluster Analysis
citations.used_for: Variance-ratio criterion; second component of the composite objective.
citations.deviation: CH is unbounded, so it cannot be averaged with a bounded index directly. It is mapped through ch/(ch+kappa) with kappa frozen from a calibration draw before the search, keeping the objective stationary.

citations.authors: Davies, D. L. & Bouldin, D. W.
citations.title: A Cluster Separation Measure
citations.used_for: Within-to-between scatter ratio; third component of the composite.
citations.deviation: Inverted to 1/(1+DB) so that, like the others, larger is better.

citations.authors: Arbelaitz, O., Gurrutxaga, I., Muguerza, J., Perez, J. M. & Perona, I.
citations.title: An Extensive Comparative Study of Cluster Validity Indices
citations.used_for: Justifying *which* three indices to use, rather than picking the familiar one.
citations.implemented_in: metrics module docstring; choice of SIL / CH / DB
citations.deviation: The study evaluates 30 indices on data with known ground truth. No ground truth exists here, so its ranking is imported as prior evidence, not re-derived.

citations.authors: Milligan, G. W. & Cooper, M. C.
citations.title: An Examination of Procedures for Determining the Number of Clusters in a Data Set
citations.used_for: The documented bias of stopping rules toward small k - the reason the objective is constrained and the k-sweep is reported in full.
citations.deviation: Their comparison is on well-separated synthetic data. On this book the bias is confirmed empirically in the k-sweep panel rather than assumed.

citations.authors: Vendramin, L., Campello, R. J. G. B. & Hruschka, E. R.
citations.title: Relative Clustering Validity Criteria: A Comparative Overview
citations.used_for: The general result that no single relative criterion dominates, motivating a weighted combination plus constraints.
citations.deviation: Weights are asserted (0.50/0.30/0.20) and stated, not learned. Sensitivity to them is bounded by the leaderboard, which shows the top configurations under the composite alongside their individual indices.

citations.authors: Ben-Hur, A., Elisseeff, A. & Guyon, I.
citations.title: A Stability Based Method for Discovering Structure in Clustered Data
citations.used_for: Resampling stability as the primary evidence that structure is real.
citations.deviation: The paper compares two independent subsamples on their overlap. Here every replicate is compared to the full-data reference partition, which is the quantity actually of interest in deployment ('would this month's refit reproduce the segments we are campaigning against?').

citations.authors: Lange, T., Roth, V., Braun, M. L. & Buhmann, J. M.
citations.title: Stability-Based Validation of Clustering Solutions
citations.used_for: Using an inductive extension of a transductive clustering to transfer labels between resamples - exactly what deployment also requires.
citations.deviation: They train a classifier as the extension operator; here it is a nearest-centroid rule, which is weaker but has no hyperparameters of its own to confound the stability estimate, and is the rule that actually ships.

citations.authors: von Luxburg, U.
citations.title: Clustering Stability: An Overview
citations.venue: Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning 2(3)
citations.used_for: The caution that stability is not a monotone signal for k and can be high for the wrong reasons.
citations.implemented_in: evaluate.k_sweep (stability reported per k, never used alone)
citations.deviation: Treated as one of three converging lines of evidence for k, alongside the constrained objective and the gap statistic.

citations.authors: Hennig, C.
citations.title: Cluster-wise Assessment of Cluster Stability
citations.used_for: Per-cluster bootstrap Jaccard and the 0.60 / 0.85 interpretation bands (SC-2) - a partition can be stable on average and still contain a segment that dissolves.
citations.deviation: Subsampling without replacement rather than the bootstrap, to avoid duplicate points inflating the apparent compactness of a cluster.

citations.authors: Hubert, L. & Arabie, P.
citations.title: Comparing Partitions
citations.used_for: Adjusted Rand Index for partition agreement across resamples.
citations.deviation: None.

citations.authors: Vinh, N. X., Epps, J. & Bailey, J.
citations.title: Information Theoretic Measures for Clusterings Comparison
citations.used_for: NMI as a second agreement measure with different bias to ARI.
citations.deviation: Reported alongside ARI, not instead of it; the paper's point is precisely that the choice of measure is not neutral.

citations.authors: Tibshirani, R., Walther, G. & Hastie, T.
citations.title: Estimating the Number of Clusters in a Data Set via the Gap Statistic
citations.used_for: An independent, null-referenced read on k.
citations.deviation: Uses the paper's PCA-aligned uniform reference, with a smaller number of Monte-Carlo draws than recommended for budget reasons; s_k is reported so the resulting uncertainty is visible.

citations.authors: Lawson, R. G. & Jurs, P. C.
citations.title: New Index for Clustering Tendency and its Application to Chemical Problems
citations.venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Computer Sciences 30(1)
citations.used_for: Testing before modelling whether the data is clusterable at all.
citations.deviation: Sampling-based estimate over a 5% sample; the statistic is sensitive to the sampling window, so it is read as a coarse go/no-go, not a p-value.

citations.authors: Fraley, C. & Raftery, A. E.
citations.title: How Many Clusters? Which Clustering Method? Answers Via Model-Based Cluster Analysis
citations.used_for: Model-based clustering as a family with a different inductive bias to k-means (elliptical, unequal-covariance clusters).
citations.deviation: Model selection is by the shared composite objective rather than BIC, so that every algorithm in the zoo is judged on identical terms.

citations.authors: Campello, R. J. G. B., Moulavi, D. & Sander, J.
citations.title: Density-Based Clustering Based on Hierarchical Density Estimates
citations.used_for: A density family that can decline to assign points, as a check on whether the partition-forcing families are inventing structure.
citations.deviation: Noise fraction is penalised in the objective: an unassigned account still has to receive a treatment, so a solution that abstains on a third of the book is not usable however clean the remainder looks.

citations.authors: von Luxburg, U.
citations.title: A Tutorial on Spectral Clustering
citations.used_for: A graph-based family able to find non-convex structure.
citations.deviation: Guarded above n=3,000 because the eigendecomposition is super-linear; it therefore competes only during the subsampled search, which is stated rather than left implicit.

citations.authors: Zhang, T., Ramakrishnan, R. & Livny, M.
citations.title: BIRCH: An Efficient Data Clustering Method for Very Large Databases
citations.used_for: A single-pass hierarchical method as the scalability reference point.
citations.deviation: None.

citations.authors: Craven, M. W. & Shavlik, J. W.
citations.title: Extracting Tree-Structured Representations of Trained Networks
citations.used_for: The surrogate-tree pattern and, critically, the distinction between fidelity to the model and accuracy against truth.
citations.deviation: A plain CART surrogate rather than TREPAN's oracle-queried induction; the training set is large enough that querying an oracle for synthetic points adds little.

citations.authors: van der Maaten, L. & Hinton, G.
citations.title: Visualizing Data using t-SNE
